newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen unsettled with Dow, Iraq nerves.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen unsettled with Dow, Iraq nerves.

text.p: German shares were seen unsettled and susceptible to profit-taking with a lower Dow Jones open and on fears that Iraqi missiles fired at U.S. jets could heighten tensions between Washington and Baghdad.
The IBIS DAX index of all-day electronic trade was quoted 8.53 points lower at 2,560.24, while September DAX futures were down 10 points at 2,563, close to day-lows.
"The market's been overbought, the dollar's been overbought and people are starting to take profits," said one dealer.
Traders said the market dipped on news of new Iraqi attacks on U.S. jets but not as sharply as last week's conflict.
Wall Street's early weakness after a profit-warning from U.S. electronics group Motorola and a slight easing of dollar levels against the mark also contributed to the decline in German shares.

"The market is looking for somewhere new to go. The U.S. figures on Thursday and Friday will be looked at closely," said one trader referring to August U.S. producer prices due Thursday at 1230 GMT, money supply data after the German market close at 2030 GMT and Friday's consumer prices figures.
Dollar-linked stocks shed most of their early strengths, with only chemical group Hoechst making significant ground.
Hoechst shares stood 55 pfennigs higher at 53.45, down from an earlier day-high on IBIS of 53.70.
Shares in Volkswagen were 90 pfennigs up at 562.70. VW chief Ferdinand Piech early on Wednesday said he wanted to boost the car-maker's productivity by 30 percent.
The comments come after a recent interview with Piech that he was seeking in the coming years to secure a ten-fold increase in VW's current return on sales level.
